title: A billion seconds is almost 32 years
summary: One billion seconds is about 31.7 years and one trillion seconds is about 31,700 years, using the 365.25 day year of 31,557,600 seconds.

beats.say: A billion seconds is almost thirty two years.

data.verdict: Three zeros, a thousand times longer

beats.say: A second is defined by counting cycles of light from a caesium atom.
A day holds eighty six thousand four hundred of them.
The astronomers' year is three hundred sixty five and a quarter days.
That year is about thirty one and a half million seconds.
A billion seconds divided by that is thirty one point seven years.
A trillion seconds is a thousand times longer.
That is about thirty one thousand seven hundred years.
Each extra three zeros multiplies the time by a thousand.
A billion is a human lifetime. A trillion is a geological one.

claims.note: BIPM: the second is 9 192 631 770 periods of the caesium-133 hyperfine transition radiation

facts.claim: The SI second is the duration of 9,192,631,770 periods of the radiation from the caesium-133 hyperfine transition
facts.note: BIPM, SI base unit second: caesium frequency fixed at 9 192 631 770 Hz; one second is 9 192 631 770 periods

facts.claim: The Julian year is exactly 365.25 days, or 31,557,600 seconds
facts.note: Britannica, Lengths of years and months: Julian year is 365.25 d, or 31,557,600 s

facts.claim: Before 1960 the second was defined as 1/86,400 of the mean solar day
facts.note: Hong Kong ITC SI page, history table: before 1960, the fraction 1/86 400 of the mean solar day
